# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. Current representative adapter observations are supplied in docs/evidence/adapter.json; reuse them where sufficient.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library, sqlite3, existing adapter 2.3. No new dependencies.

## Structure

src/adapter.py stays the row application interface. Proposed src/inventory.py owns argparse CLI; proposed src/batch_import.py owns validation, isolated snapshot, publication and recovery. tests/test_baseline.py stays unchanged; planned tests/process_fixture.py owns test-only control and tests/test_batch_import.py owns automated batch checks. New modules resolve as src.inventory and src.batch_import from repository root; package src/__init__.py already exists and has no conflicting exports. Only src.inventory is a public module entrypoint; batch helper exports import_batch. No remote namespace exists. data/ is retained read-only seed input.

## Conventions

Small explicit functions and unittest, matching src/adapter.py and tests/test_baseline.py. All temporary probes and test databases live under the sibling run/scratch directory.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Proposed command: python3 -B -m src.inventory import-json --db PATH --file PATH. Stdout JSON {"accepted":2} only after success; nonzero and stderr on failure. JSON is a list of exact sku/quantity records; default reject duplicate SKUs, empty/blank sku, bool quantities, unknown fields and integers outside SQLite signed 64-bit. Empty batch is a successful no-op. These defaults require CLI documentation and tests; they do not change the adapter API.

## Real-boundary checks

Only local boundaries apply. No deployed target, browser, service, authorization or account outcome is observable or needed. sqlite3 queries in a fresh process/connection are the inventory consumer; CLI subprocess exit/stdout/stderr is the command consumer. In-process mocks alone cannot prove publication/recovery behavior.

RB-1 (planned; batch implementation owner; due test): create isolated B and input V specified in environment.md; invoke CLI with concrete fixture paths; observe exit 0 and accepted=2, open DB independently and compare all sorted rows to N; repeat and assert N. Preserves unrelated old SKU while updating same. Before state, input, action and oracle have been manually walked; no execution claim.

RB-2 (planned; same owner/due): begin at fresh B for every case, apply invalid-middle input or adapter error; require nonzero/no success and B with fresh observer immediately and after recovery. Supplied adapter evidence proves the direct-write negative control fails, not that staging succeeds.

RB-3 (planned; same owner/due): controlled actual child stops at named implementation boundaries before publication, during publication, during recovery and after publication before acknowledgement. Parent kills/reaps it, then independently queries visible rows BEFORE running recovery, repeats recovery and queries again. An interrupted uncommitted import must retain B, never mixed rows. If any proposed protocol exposes N after a kill that the requirement calls an interrupted import, keep that conflict open and revise the protocol or obtain an explicit user interpretation; do not silently redefine interruption as only pre-publication. Planning must identify its linearization/acknowledgement boundary and residual impossibility limits.

RB-4 (planned; same owner/due): use SQLite backup/snapshot and publication experiments only on disposable databases to establish existing-state/schema preservation, WAL handling, failure cleanup and same-directory replacement assumptions. Snapshot experiments are supporting platform evidence, not acceptance tests. Filesystem crash/power-loss durability beyond process interruption has no established target or guarantee and must not be claimed.

Target reset: each case starts with a new fixture directory and independently created B, not residual state left by a prior pass. No concurrent writer behavior required. No case writes retained seed inventory. Recovery fixtures must correspond to reachable protocol states; arbitrary invented marker files cannot establish reachability.

## Decisions

AD-4: Place CLI in src.inventory, import_batch validation/staging/publication in src.batch_import, and test-only process control in tests.process_fixture. Reuse existing src and tests packages; avoid empty scaffolds. Status: planned. Alternative: changing adapter.py would entangle its preserved API and still not solve its separate commits.
AD-5: Authoritative data stays in local SQLite inventory(sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY, quantity INTEGER). No new persistent schema or migration is planned. Stage contains validated batch, owned by importer and safely cleaned on failure/recovery; cleanup must prove ownership with a private directory identity marker, never delete guessed residue or SQLite sidecars. Use explicit atomic destination transaction transferring staged values while preserving unrelated records and auxiliary schema; only an initially absent path uses completed same-directory staged-file replacement. Alternative complete-file replacement carries sidecar and identity risks. Status: current-runtime primitive confirmed by E1/E2 in the Plan Improve investigation; product implementation/tests remain due, and AD-6 semantic gate is unresolved. No power-loss certification, multiwriter policy or quota target is asserted.
AD-6: Local actor calls synchronous CLI -> standard-library importer -> staged installed adapter -> SQLite publication -> JSON success. No queue, polling, cache, network, server or account. Failures reach caller through nonzero/status and stderr. A lost success acknowledgement requires state read/retry and cannot itself prove rollback. Status: proposed interruption interpretation remains open; request is unchanged and postcommit ambiguity gates W2 as described in RUN/notes/batch-plan.md.
AD-7: Protect retained data/ paths and symlink aliases before writes; all fixtures/probes use owned scratch. Existing schema changes require a correction rather than silent replacement. No personal-data collection, remote logs, secret/config store or unbounded retention is introduced. Status: planned, due W2 negative path checks.

AD-1: Preserve standard-library stack, installed adapter and existing baseline; accepted.
AD-2: Never apply the adapter directly to the visible inventory for a batch. Supplied exact-configuration evidence docs/evidence/adapter.json proves partial writes. Apply the batch on a disposable isolated stage, then transfer its complete rows inside one explicit destination transaction; unrelated rows stay in place. Current primitive confirmation is recorded in the bound Plan Improve investigation; product publication/recovery tests remain due. Adapter replacement is not justified by its commit behavior alone.
AD-3: All CLI and recovery acceptance remains planned. Definition, runtime readiness, primitive experiments and product acceptance are distinct evidence.

## Superseded

The seed's mention of search responsibility is outside this request and removed. No search work is authorized.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python 3.9.6, SQLite 3.54.0, standard library only. Execution root is the owned worktree. Fresh readiness evidence: RUN/scratch/baseline-current.json (RUN is the sibling run directory). No browser, deployment, account, external endpoint or credentials are required or authorized. No concurrent writers; observers reopen SQLite connections between commands. Do not open retained data for writes. Every test creates its own database under RUN/scratch via TemporaryDirectory; remove only owned fixtures.

## Commands

Current full regression and bounded smoke (one existing case; <1 second): from the worktree, with TMPDIR set to the absolute sibling run/scratch directory:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
Observed exit 0, one case `test_single_row_roundtrip`; not feature acceptance. After implementation the same discovery command must register all new cases and print their names; expected cost <30 seconds, including process interruption checks.

Current focused baseline (<1 second):
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_baseline -v
```
Includes only `test_single_row_roundtrip`; same disposable fixture prerequisites.

Planned focused batch suite, not executable until its implementation prerequisite is complete:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_batch_import -v
```
Must print test_TC_1 through test_TC_9 as declared below. Planned bounded smoke (<5 seconds):

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_batch_import.BatchImport.test_TC_1 tests.test_batch_import.BatchImport.test_TC_2 -v
```
Includes only CLI success and invalid-middle cases; not recovery or full regression evidence. These future commands remain NOT-REPLAYED because the module does not exist. ## Skills

## Harnesses and suites

Extend unittest, with no dependencies or coverage download. All are planned, not passed. ### Requirement mapping and fixture oracles
